skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Mask-driven image inpainting on RunComfy via the `runcomfy` CLI. Routes to Tongyi MAI Z-Image Turbo Inpainting (the dedicated inpainting endpoint with mask, strength, and control-scale) and to identity-preserving edit models (Nano Banana 2 Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, FLUX Kontext Pro) when a mask isn't available and the region must be described instead. Use for object removal, watermark removal, region replacement, blemish cleanup, and any controlled local edit where a binary mask defines the target area. Triggers on "inpaint", "inpainting", "image inpaint", "remove from image", "fill region", "mask-driven edit", "remove watermark", "remove object", "patch the photo", "fill the hole", or any explicit ask to edit a specific masked region of a still.
skill.summary: Edit selected image regions through RunComfy using masks or descriptions, with guidance for model selection and preservation.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: All 77 static matches are false positives involving Markdown, documentation links, example URLs, standard token storage, or model-selection advice. One semantic finding identifies misleading shell-safety guidance that could encourage unsafe command construction. No evidence found of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection; the external CLI implementation was not included.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:207 incorrectly treats JSON input as sufficient protection against shell injection.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the blanket assurance and require shell-free argument passing or correct shell escaping of serialized JSON, including apostrophes in prompts and URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Misleading Shell-Injection Safety Assurance
semantic_findings.description: Line 207 claims "No shell-injection surface" because inputs are JSON. Interpolating untrusted text into the single-quoted shell examples without shell escaping can allow command injection before the CLI receives JSON.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The blanket assurance ignores shell parsing before CLI execution. The literal examples are safe as written; exploitation depends on unsafe substitution of untrusted input.

content.user_title: Edit Image Regions with Masks or Descriptions
content.value_statement: Local image edits need clear targeting and preservation constraints. This skill guides RunComfy model selection and CLI requests for masked inpainting or description-based edits.
actual_capabilities: Routes masked image edits to Z-Image Turbo Inpainting through the RunComfy CLI.
Provides object-removal and background-replacement request examples with source image and mask URLs.
Explains strength, control scale, aspect ratio, and seed inputs for masked edits.
Uses Nano Banana 2 Edit as a description-based fallback when no mask is available.
Provides selection guidance for LoRA inpainting, GPT Image 2 Edit, and FLUX Kontext Pro.
Documents output-directory downloads and CLI exit codes for troubleshooting.
limitations: Requires a separately installed RunComfy CLI, authentication, network access, and available hosted model endpoints.
Does not create masks; masked inpainting requires a user-supplied image URL and grayscale mask URL.
Does not cover canvas outpainting or video inpainting.
Generated results require review; exact preservation outside the target region is not guaranteed.

use_cases.title: Retouch Street Photographs
use_cases.description: Remove masked overhead cables while requesting preservation of rooflines, lighting, and surrounding sky.

use_cases.title: Replace Product Backgrounds
use_cases.description: Replace a masked product backdrop with a studio background while requesting preservation of the product.

use_cases.title: Plan Brand-Style Region Edits
use_cases.description: Select the LoRA inpainting variant for masked edits using an existing brand-style adapter.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Remove a Masked Object
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [image URL] and [mask URL] to remove overhead cables. Preserve rooflines and sky. Start with strength 0.5 and control scale 0.8.
prompt_templates.scenario: A source image and matching mask are ready.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace the background in [image URL] using [background mask URL]. Use smooth light gray studio paper and strength 0.9. Preserve the product.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product photo needs a new background.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Edit Without a Mask
prompt_templates.prompt: No mask is available for [image URL]. Use Nano Banana 2 Edit to remove [object and location]. Request preservation of everything else.
prompt_templates.scenario: The target region can be described clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Configure a Reproducible Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an inpainting request for [image URL] and [mask URL] with seed [integer], strength [value], and control scale [value]. Explain preservation tradeoffs before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced user wants explicit parameter control.

output_examples.input: Remove cables from a street photo using a matching mask.
output: Illustrative request plan: Z-Image Turbo Inpainting with strength 0.5 and control scale 0.8.
Preservation request: retain rooflines and match the surrounding sky.
Review target: check filled sky and mask edges for artifacts.

output_examples.input: Replace a product background with light gray studio paper.
output: Illustrative request plan: masked background replacement with strength 0.9.
Preservation request: retain product shape, colors, and visible details.
Review target: inspect product boundaries and background consistency.

best_practices: Use a matching grayscale mask: white marks edits and black preserves regions; consider slight edge blur for blending.
Match strength to edit scope, name preservation constraints, and inspect generated results before reuse.
Use only authorized image URLs, protect API tokens, and keep untrusted inputs separate from shell command syntax.
anti_patterns: Using the mask-required endpoint without a mask or expecting this skill to generate one.
Assuming description-based editing guarantees pixel-perfect preservation outside the requested region.
Embedding untrusted prompts or URLs into shell commands without proper escaping because the payload uses JSON.

faq.question: Do I need a mask?
faq.answer: Z-Image Turbo Inpainting requires a mask. Without one, the skill recommends Nano Banana 2 Edit with a clear region description.

faq.question: Can this skill create masks?
faq.answer: No. Create a grayscale mask in an external tool and provide its URL. White marks edits; black marks preserved regions.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and authenticate with runcomfy login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN. Hosted model access and network connectivity are required.

faq.question: Are images processed locally?
faq.answer: No. The CLI submits requests to the RunComfy Model API. Use only images and masks approved for external processing.

faq.question: Does this cover video or canvas expansion?
faq.answer: No. The documentation refers video inpainting and canvas outpainting to separate skills.

faq.question: Can I guarantee unchanged pixels outside the target?
faq.answer: No. Masks and preservation instructions guide the edit, but generated outputs still require visual inspection.
